To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have analyzed mean latency of a split and replicated system under general service time distributions.

(1) under general service time distribution, a split and replicate storage system with power of $d\geq 2$ load balancing policy has a mean latency upper bounded by $\frac{2}{d}$ times that of an un-split replicated system and (2) under low redundancy regime, a coded system with fractional redundancy factor between 0 and 1 has a mean latency that is upper bounded by $\log (n)$ times that of an uncoded system with the same fractional redundancy factor

(i) under high redundancy (fractional factor greater than 2) regime the mean latency of an erasure coded and a split replicate systems are comparable, and (ii) under low redundancy (fraction 1 to 2) an erasure coded storage system has a smaller mean latency compared to a split replicate system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mean latency analysis of split and replicate systems and erasure coded systems.
latency in data centers with a large number (thousands to millions) of servers.

the following: - Mean latency analysis of large scale split and replicate storage systems with general sub exponential service times - Mean latency analysis for erasure coded storage systems under low redundancy - Numerical validation of the mean latency bounds and comparison to the mean latency of an unsplit replicate system - Tail latency analysis of large split and replicate systems with memoryless servers
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for a split and replicate (coded) system with high redundancy, the mean latency is at most a constant factor away from that of a unsplit replicated system and for a coded system with low-redundancy, the mean latency depends on the order statistic of the queue lengths.

the mean latency in a coded cloud storage system is upper bounded (up to a constant) by that of an un-split replicated system, for any sub-exponential distribution and any redundancy regime, and that the gap is small (at least 20%) in practice.

, for the mean latency, split and replicate is the best option for high redundancy, and erasure coding with low redundancy is the best option when storage is a constraint, and for the tail latency, erasure coding is the best option, for both high and low redundancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a general framework for analyzing mean latency for split and replicate systems with general sub exponential service times and for low redundancy coded systems with exponential service times.

we provide a novel scheduling scheme for a split and replicated system and show that the mean latency of an erasure coded cloud storage system under high and low redundancy regime is upper bounded by a constant times that of the split and replicate system.
we provide a novel scheduling scheme for split and replicate storage systems under general service time distributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mean latency for a split and replicate and an erasure coded storage system is comparable and in some regimes, the coded system out performs the unsplit replication.
, for a large number of files, the mean access latency in split and replicate cloud systems with general service time distribution can be analyzed and upper bounded.
the mean latency of the coded system is upperbounded by that of the replicated system with same redundancy factor, for all practical service time distributions.
